content: Daflon 500 is also marketed under the names Detralex, Arvenum 500, Alvenor, Ardium, Capiven, Elatec, and Venitol. Presentation and Composition: Each tablet of Daflon 500 contains 500 mg of Micronized Purified Flavonoid Fraction, which is composed of 450 mg of diosmin and 50 mg of flavonoids expressed as hesperidin. Therapeutic Properties: Daflon 500 functions as a vascular protector and venotonic agent. It improves the venous return system by reducing venous distensibility and venous stasis. In the microcirculation, it helps normalize capillary permeability and strengthens capillary resistance. Pharmacokinetics: The micronization process of Daflon 500 enhances its gastrointestinal absorption compared to non-micronized diosmin. This is evidenced by a higher urinary excretion rate (57.9% for micronized diosmin versus 32.7% for non-micronized diosmin). Therapeutic Indications: Daflon 500 is indicated for the treatment of chronic venous disease of the lower limbs, whether organic or idiopathic in origin. Symptoms it addresses include heavy legs, pain, nocturnal cramps, and edema. It is also used for the treatment of hemorrhoids, including acute hemorrhoidal attacks. Side Effects: Some patients have reported minor gastrointestinal and autonomic disturbances. However, these side effects have not necessitated discontinuation of the treatment. Drug Interactions: No drug interactions have been identified. Precautions: Pregnancy: Animal studies have not shown any teratogenic effects, and no harmful effects have been reported in humans to date. Lactation: Since there is no data on whether the drug is excreted in breast milk, breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment. Contraindications: There are no known contraindications for Daflon 500. Dosage and Administration: For chronic venous disease: The recommended dose is 2 tablets per day. For hemorrhoidal disease: In acute crises: Take 6 tablets daily for 4 days, followed by 4 tablets daily for the next 3 days. For chronic treatment: Take 2 tablets per day.
